problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,1\le y\le 2}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=3(x+y).$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=1.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}3(x+y)|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}3(x+y)(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{3(x+y)^{2}}{2}(x-1)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3((x+2)^{2}-(x+1)^{2})}{2}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+3)(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}((\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}-2+3)-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{7}{6}) \\  & =\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
